title: Witness-Carrying Frontier Certificates Control Long First-Row Gaps
novelty_claim: The novel claim is not merely that skipped intervals are covered by A_n B_n, but that the endogenous mex-coupled evolution of the border sets may admit a compact certificate language for consecutive frontier coverage. If that certificate language exists or provably fails, the mechanism is specific to this array rather than generic multiplication-table density.
closest_prior_art: OEIS A129258 and A129259, Kimberling's Problem 18, and Ford-style multiplication-table / divisor-in-an-interval work as the nearest overlap branch.
differentiation: This direction only survives if each skipped integer in a record gap is explained using witness structure that depends essentially on the self-generated row and column borders, witness multiplicity, and row-vs-column assignment. Generic product-set counting or prime-gap narration is not enough.
easiest_falsifier: Log witness data for new record gaps and test whether long gaps reduce to a small reusable certificate family. If witness types sprawl, or if the same explanatory power comes from generic local product coverage without using the greedy coupling, this direction is too derivative.
evidence_plan: Required next artifact is a witness-carrying record-gap corpus: for each skipped integer in each record interval, store at least one border witness, witness multiplicity, skipped-prime flag, and any relevant row/column prime assignment. Then test whether a compact certificate taxonomy predicts or obstructs long covered intervals better than global density counts.
budget_envelope: Champion line. One focused sprint after this synthesis: one reproducible witness-carrying benchmark pass plus one targeted prior-art clearance against OEIS/Kimberling and Ford only if divisor-interval language is invoked.

title: Coupled Prime-Index Support with Odious Exponents Governs Gap Growth
novelty_claim: Row 1 is not just a mex sequence: OEIS notes indicate a multiplicative semigroup generated by row primes with odious exponents, and the row-prime indices are recursively selected from the opposite side. The potentially novel object is the coupled prime-index operator, not the prime split alone.
closest_prior_art: OEIS comments around the first-row sequence and the associated prime-support sequences, plus generic multiplicative-semigroup and prime-gap heuristics.
differentiation: Treat the row-side and column-side prime-index supports as the first-class state and ask whether their induced semigroup statistics control record gaps. This differs from a prime-gap story because it must explain composite-only record intervals and use the odious/evil exponent rule explicitly.
easiest_falsifier: Test whether fluctuations in prime-support state predict record gaps any better than direct frontier witness data. If the support layer does not add explanatory power, or if composite-only record gaps remain opaque, this abstraction is secondary at best.
evidence_plan: Do not treat this as a proof program yet. First define the exact support observables to log on the same record-gap corpus used by H1, then compare support fluctuations against skipped-prime count, witness multiplicity, and row/column offset. Promote only if the support layer explains failures that the frontier-certificate layer misses.
budget_envelope: Backup line. One narrow modeling pass only after the frontier witness corpus exists; no standalone exploration unless the primary line produces a clean support-dependent obstruction.

title: The Border Sets Form a Canonical Near-Minimal Multiplicative Basis with Unbounded Gaps
novelty_claim: The bridge claim is that the greedy mex coupling drives the border sets into a near-minimal multiplicative-basis regime, with row and column counts near 2x/log x and unbounded first-row gaps as a consequence.
closest_prior_art: Multiplicative bases of order 2, the multiplication-table problem, and divisor-in-an-interval literature.
differentiation: This line is only defensible if the greedy coupling yields a theorem or obstruction unavailable from generic sparse product-set heuristics. Without an endogenous invariant tied to the mex recursion, it is mostly a reformulation of known overlap branches.
easiest_falsifier: Check whether every claimed phenomenon can already be narrated by generic product-set density or divisor-interval heuristics. If yes, or if the line produces only asymptotic curve fitting without proof-oriented diagnostics, exclude it as overlap-heavy.
evidence_plan: Do not actively advance this line unless the primary witness-certificate program exposes a genuinely T-specific obstruction. If revisited, it must state exactly what survives direct comparison with Ford-style machinery and why record gaps are not just generic sparse-basis artifacts.
budget_envelope: De-prioritized. No active budget beyond citation clearance and one overlap check if a later draft invokes multiplication-table language.
